\ednentry{
  id = {EDN-68},
  title = {The Great Expectations store is generated and cached},
  note = {\textbf{Absorbs EDN-77} (2026-10-06): fill rates are asserted by the suites, not by the raw contract.},
  date = {2026-10-05},
  milestone = {M3: Quality Assurance},
  topic = {Data Validation, Testing Strategy},
  participants = {@lukas2510},
  decision = {The \texttt{configure\_\allowbreak{}gx} stage rebuilds the Great Expectations context under \texttt{gx/\allowbreak{}} from code, \texttt{schema.\allowbreak{}py} and \texttt{params.\allowbreak{}yaml} on every run.
\texttt{gx/\allowbreak{}} is a DVC-cached output and is not committed.
The suites' column, dtype and non-null checks are generated from \texttt{schema.\allowbreak{}py}.
Fill rates are tolerant rules in both suites, and the contracts keep only structural nullability.
Any failed expectation fails \texttt{validate-\allowbreak{}data}.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item Commit \texttt{gx/\allowbreak{}} as configuration, as the course demo does: Great Expectations writes fresh ids on every save, so two builds of the same code differ and every rerun is a diff.
\item No store, an ephemeral context: no \texttt{configure\_\allowbreak{}gx} stage and no inspectable suites.
\item Fill rates as non-null columns of the raw contract: a gap in a scrape would stop \texttt{download} like a bug in our code.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} An artefact that changes on every rebuild without changing its meaning is a build product, and we track build products with DVC.
Generating the structural checks keeps \texttt{schema.\allowbreak{}py} the one place the contract is written.
Both suites require a minimum row count, so no suite passes on an empty frame.},
  ai = {Information seeking, Alternative generation, Alternative assessment, Recommendation, Solution generation},
  response = {Accepted with modifications},
  assessment = {Before building, AI tested whether Great Expectations can bound a text date (it cannot), what the store writes across two builds, and whether each rule can hold at its place in the pipeline.
Each result changed the design; the second turned ``commit \texttt{gx/\allowbreak{}}'' into a cached output.
Lukas confirmed the setup as proposed.
An independent AI review then found four faults, among them rules that passed on an empty frame; all were fixed before merging.},
  aievidence = {Claude Code sessions of 2026-10-05 (issue \#25, review of PR \#76) and 2026-10-06 (issue \#78).},
  evidence = {\href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/blob/main/recommenditos/data/gx_context_configuration.py}{\texttt{gx\_\allowbreak{}context\_\allowbreak{}configuration.\allowbreak{}py}}, \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/blob/main/reports/analysis/gx_probe_results.txt}{\texttt{gx\_\allowbreak{}probe\_\allowbreak{}results.\allowbreak{}txt}}, \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/pull/76}{PR \#76}, \href{https://github.com/mlops-2627q1-mds-upc/MLOPS_Recommenditos/issues/78}{issue \#78}.},
